chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr and Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'How much is the dower, meaning in the Mut'a?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Whatever they both agree upon, up to whatever they so desire from the term'.
ai.seo_question: What is the rule for determining the amount of dower in Shia temporary marriage (Mut'a)?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the chain of prominent Kufi scholars including Asim ibn Hamid, clarifies that the dower in Mut'a is entirely subject to mutual consent (taradi) without statutory limits, distinguishing it from permanent marriage where certain conditions apply. It underscores the flexibility of temporary marriage contracts in Shia jurisprudence, allowing the parties to negotiate the financial terms freely for the agreed duration. This ruling is foundational for understanding the economic aspects of Mut'a as a distinct contractual relationship.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, and Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Najran, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from Muhammad Bin Muslim
who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws, ‘How much is the dower, meaning in the Mut’a?’ Heasws said: ‘Whatever they both agree upon, up to whatever they so desire to from the term’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr and ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn abu Najran from ‘Asem ibn Hamid from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “In response to my question before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about how much mahr (dower) is - in al-Mut‘ah (advantageous marriage), he (the Imam) said, ‘It is whatever they agree on, up to the time they want.’”
